answer: Stake-bonded reputation resists Sybils: each agent identity must lock a refundable bond and earn trust only through verified completed work, starting with tight rate limits. Like a juniper rooting slowly in tundra soil, reputation grows gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker creating thousands of fake identities must fund every bond and wait out the same slow maturation, while a public ledger acts as a river carrying each attestation downstream for all to audit. Misbehavior slashes the bond and erases the history, so fake identities cost capital and time instead of being free.
